subject: pathology
title: Myeloproliferative neoplasms and myelodysplastic syndromes

steps.tx: **Myeloproliferative neoplasms** are clonal stem cell disorders where the marrow overproduces mature blood cells over time. Polycythaemia vera increases red cells, essential thrombocythaemia increases platelets, and primary myelofibrosis replaces marrow with fibrosis. The **JAK2 V617F** mutation drives most cases because it switches on signalling without normal growth factor control. CALR and MPL mutations explain many cases where JAK2 testing returns negative in clinic.
steps.say: Myeloproliferative neoplasms are clonal disorders where stem cells overproduce mature blood cells without normal regulatory control. JAK2 signalling is central because this mutation activates growth pathways continuously in the marrow clone. Different phenotypes develop because the clone expands mainly red cells, platelets or fibrotic marrow tissue.

steps.tx: **Polycythaemia vera** increases red cell mass while erythropoietin levels fall because the clone grows without hormonal drive. Patients report aquagenic itching after showers, burning erythromelalgia in the feet, gout and thrombosis in unusual veins. Hepatic vein thrombosis causing **Budd Chiari syndrome** is a classic presentation that examiners favour in stems. Venesection and antiplatelet therapy reduce thrombotic risk, while secondary erythrocytosis shows raised erythropoietin from hypoxia or tumours.
steps.say: Polycythaemia vera is a clonal disease where red cell mass rises while erythropoietin levels become suppressed appropriately. Aquagenic itching is characteristic because patients notice intense itching after warm showers or baths. Hormone measurement helps clinicians separate true vera from secondary causes driven by hypoxia.

steps.tx: **Primary myelofibrosis** replaces normal marrow with reticulin and collagen, so blood production shifts to spleen and liver. This extramedullary production causes massive splenomegaly, while squeezed red cells become teardrop shaped **dacrocytes** in blood. The film also shows a **leukoerythroblastic picture** with nucleated red cells and immature myeloid precursors escaping the fibrotic marrow. Dry tap on aspiration supports the diagnosis, and transformation to acute leukaemia worsens prognosis greatly.
steps.say: Primary myelofibrosis is a disease where marrow becomes fibrotic and blood production moves into the spleen instead. Teardrop cells appear because red cells are squeezed through fibrotic marrow and splenic tissue during release. Dry tap occurs because the aspirate needle cannot withdraw liquid marrow from fibrotic tissue.

right.title: Secondary erythrocytosis
points: Treat the hypoxic or tumour cause

steps.tx: This blood smear shows teardrop shaped **dacrocytes** together with nucleated red cells and immature myeloid precursors in circulation. That combination forms a **leukoerythroblastic picture**, which points strongly towards marrow fibrosis rather than simple anaemia. In **primary myelofibrosis** the fibrotic marrow forces blood production into the spleen, causing massive splenomegaly and constitutional symptoms. Examiners use this film because one image captures the morphology, mechanism and likely marrow aspiration difficulty.
steps.say: This smear shows teardrop cells because fibrotic marrow distorts red cells as they leave the marrow space. Leukoerythroblastic features appear because nucleated red cells and immature myeloid cells escape into blood early. This film helps clinicians suspect myelofibrosis before marrow biopsy confirms the fibrosis.

vis.alt: Blood smear with teardrop dacrocytes, nucleated red cell and immature myeloid precursors.
vis.caption: Teardrop cells with leukoerythroblastic features in myelofibrosis. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Myelodysplastic syndromes** are clonal marrow disorders where production is ineffective despite a cellular marrow in older adults. Dysplastic cells die inside the marrow, so cytopenias develop even though precursors appear numerous on biopsy. **Ring sideroblasts**, blast percentage and cytogenetic abnormalities grade the risk of progression towards acute myeloid leukaemia. The **5q deletion syndrome** causes macrocytic anaemia with lobated megakaryocytes and responds uniquely well to lenalidomide therapy.
steps.say: Myelodysplastic syndromes are disorders where clonal marrow produces dysplastic cells that fail to mature into blood properly. Cytopenias develop because ineffective production destroys precursors before they reach the peripheral circulation successfully. Blast percentage helps clinicians grade risk because higher counts predict progression towards acute leukaemia.

vis.alt: Microscopic view of myelodysplastic syndrome bone marrow showing dysplastic cells like ring sideroblasts and lobated megakaryocytes, indicating ineffective hematopoiesis.
vis.caption: MDS: dysplastic, ineffective cells despite cellular marrow. Image: Paulo Henrique Orlandi Mourao, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: **Chronic myeloid leukaemia** is driven by the BCR ABL1 fusion gene on the **Philadelphia chromosome** in stem cells. The disease causes marked leukocytosis with basophilia and splenomegaly because granulocyte production expands massively over time. **Imatinib** blocks the abnormal tyrosine kinase and transforms survival for most patients with this disease. Mastocytosis and clonal hypereosinophilic disorders complete the proliferative family that examiners sample less frequently in papers.
steps.say: Chronic myeloid leukaemia is a disease where the Philadelphia chromosome creates an abnormal kinase that drives granulocyte production. Imatinib treatment is effective because it blocks that kinase directly inside the leukaemic clone cells. Basophilia helps clinicians suspect this diagnosis when leukocytosis appears with splenomegaly in stems.
